A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FlowDirector and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. The shared editing framework and retained examples support reliable comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original quantitative baseline comparisons, qualitative editing results, component ablations, and an appendix efficiency comparison.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark results, quantitative component ablations, parameter studies, runtime and memory measurements, and qualitative results for two model sizes.

M1.justification: V2 adds Direction-Aware Flow Correction through velocity decomposition and Motion-Appearance Decoupling through a motion-energy correction. DAG changes from averaging differences against subset estimates to selecting the least cosine-aligned candidates, and late-stage noise is frozen. V1's attention masking and edge softening remain within the revised framework; they are not newly introduced.

E1.justification: V1 describes Internet and Wan-generated videos; v2 explicitly evaluates Internet/DAVIS pairs. Demonstrated coverage expands to black-and-white colorization, prolonged occlusion, and combined identity/gesture changes (Figures 4 and 20–22). These introduce substantive task and input-condition coverage beyond the retained object, material, and local-attribute edits.

E2.justification: The five main baselines remain FateZero, FLATTEN, TokenFlow, RAVE, and VideoDirector. However, the appendix efficiency comparison expands beyond DAG versus conventional averaging to measured FLATTEN, TokenFlow, and RAVE comparisons in v2 Table 4. FateZero and VideoDirector have missing measurements there because of memory limits.

E3.justification: Main evaluation changes from 8/22/36 to 41/81 frames, removes Frame-Acc, and adds a 14B configuration. V2 uses all 50 denoising steps instead of skipping ten, disables source CFG previously set to 3.5, and changes mask smoothing from 11 to 9. Its principal DAG setting uses three rather than four samples, although Appendix F still describes four. Efficiency testing changes from four 4090 GPUs to one H800.

E4.justification: V2 adds quantitative component-removal and DA-FC strength ablations (Tables 2–3), motion-correction case studies, attention-block comparisons, and sensitivity studies for motion-correction parameters, DAG strength, and ensemble sizes. It expands efficiency analysis with memory measurements and source-CFG discussion. V1's dedicated SAFC ablation and Porsche WarpError case analysis disappear; the DAG averaging and incomplete-prompt examples remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seed counts, repeated-trial uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The changing numbers of stochastic DAG samples concern the inference procedure, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the earlier scores with results under different video lengths and evaluation settings. For example, 1.3B CLIP-T changes from 33.72/33.79/33.84 for 8/22/36 frames to 34.64/34.63 for 41/81 frames; this does not establish a same-setting gain. V2 adds 14B, quantitative ablation, and resource results, while removing Frame-Acc entries and the Porsche WarpError table.

T1.justification: V2 introduces the formal parallel/orthogonal decomposition and piecewise correction in Equations 5–6, plus motion residuals, an energy function, and an approximate gradient update in Equations 9–11. Its DAG definition also changes substantively: selecting least-aligned candidates avoids the cancellation implied by averaging all subset differences in v1 Equations 5–7. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contribution changes from direct ODE editing with spatial masking and semantic guidance to three corrections targeting appearance transformation, motion preservation, and stability. Abstract and conclusion add explicit motion-energy and variance-reduction claims. V1's explicit claim to be the first inversion-free editing work using pretrained T2V models is dropped.

C2.justification: V2 attributes stronger transformations to directional correction and reframes DAG primarily around noise suppression and trajectory stability, rather than overcoming structural-preservation bias. It adds interpretations of skipping versus full sampling, motion/appearance tradeoffs, and why DAG's visible benefits yield modest metric gains. The incomplete-prompt failure and limited style-transfer applicability are retained.

D1.justification: V2 supplies full inference pseudocode instead of mask-only pseudocode, documents attention aggregation and upsampling, and adds timestep-shift, correction, and noise-schedule settings plus hardware/memory information. However, v1's explicit 832x480 resolution is omitted. Reproducibility remains weakened by three-versus-four DAG sample descriptions and the reversed anchor-difference sign between Equation 11 and Algorithm 1. Code release remains promised through the same project link.

R1.justification: The related-work organization and principal editing references remain. V2 adds DAVIS and a FlowAlign discussion, although FlowAlign has an unresolved citation, and removes several dataset and guidance references, including classifier-free guidance and guiding with a bad model. The explicit first-work positioning is softened without changing the overall research area.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method narrative, ablation discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Appendices are reorganized around full inference and separate correction analyses, while Broader Impacts and the standalone extended baseline-comparison section disappear. The author list and affiliations also change.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout, replaces the original framework diagram with trajectory and vector diagrams, restructures Table 1, and adds ablation tables, attention maps, and parameter-study figures. Qualitative montages are substantially rearranged and refreshed. The earlier DAG and prompt-failure figures are retained with relocation and formatting changes.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens methodological coherence and empirical support: its selected-baseline DAG avoids the cancellation in v1's written formulation, while Tables 2–3 provide quantitative component evidence previously supported largely by qualitative examples. Motion-focused cases, sensitivity studies, and resource measurements further substantiate the revised framework. These gains outweigh reporting regressions, although the MAD-FC equation/pseudocode disagreement, inconsistent DAG sample descriptions, and omitted resolution still impede reproducibility. Changed evaluation conditions prevent interpreting the new headline scores as direct performance improvements over v1.
